findings.text: non-blocking: the gate reading is described as 'on the committed tree', but logs/gate-coordinator.log:1 names revision 2abb60a10, whose tree holds 83 cases and not the two this round added, and its mtime (05:22:41 +0200) precedes the commit eee6c4d2b (05:23:34 +0200) that added them; the run was taken on the working tree before the commit, so the 85-count cannot be reconciled with the revision the log names, and the log's first line also carries no tree line, which the node's own done-when requires ('with the revision, tree and command on the log's first line'). I ran the two new cases at the reviewed head and both pass (2 passed, 12 deselected), so the code is sound; a gate re-run at 29ef6788a closes the record defect.

non-blocking: the review-route paragraph claims a base arm measured 'with the base revision's tree extracted from 0409dcbe4', and reports that at that base the copy is already removed and the ledger row already carries its release block, so only the receipt distinguishes base from head; no log for that base arm exists under the run directory (logs/ holds gate.log, gate-repair.log, gate-coordinator.log and the two negative controls only), so the claim carries no receipt, against section 8's 'every log is under the run directory, and the evidence fragment quotes each gate's command and summary line'. It also means the plan's base-red clause for the review case ('leaves the scratch and no release block at the base') is not demonstrated by the landed case.

non-blocking: moving the receipt onto write_json_atomically answers the earlier reuse finding, but no added assertion reddens if it is reverted to target.write_text(...): the review case at tests/test_a_runs_scratch_is_removed_on_the_host_that_made_it.py:445 asserts the receipt exists and names the host, which a whole-file write satisfies equally. The atomicity half of this commit therefore has no test that fails on its regression.

non-blocking: the coherent-root rule is now written a second time here in a stricter form (both named, both from the environment, or both at their defaults) while garbage_collect_orphan_scratch keeps its own copy of the same rule at gc.py:1043-1052 (refuse when RECKON_HOME is set and the scratch root is not); neither calls the other and no shared predicate exists, so a later change to one will not move the other.

non-blocking: the new guard case exercises only the root-named-alone branch; the symmetric branch at gc.py:1207-1208 (runs_root named while root is left to the environment) has no assertion, so half of the three-way rule the commit introduced is unguarded.

findings_note: the earlier review's three findings are addressed in this diff: the guard docstring now states the three-way rule its code applies (gc.py:1183-1188), the receipt is written through write_json_atomically (promotion_release.py:587), and the review case drives promotion.complete rather than the release function (tests:434). The review-route finding is only half answered: the route is now driven end to end, but its base-red differential is the receipt alone and that base arm has no log (finding 2).
